content.title: NASA visibility map shows path of Artemis II splashdown today in California
content.text: April 10, 2026, 8:32 a.m. ETLive coverage of the NASA Artemis II splashdown will be at floridatoday.com/space.The Artemis II mission's Orion capsule is scheduled to splash down in the Pacific Ocean on April 10, 2026.NASA will livestream the event on its various platforms, including NASA+ and YouTube.Happy splashdown day to all who celebrate! NASA’s Artemis II crew is due to reenter Earth's atmosphere for a water landing in the Pacific Ocean. As of Friday morning, April 10, the Orion capsule carrying the Artemis II astronauts is nearing 85,000 miles from Earth, leaving the moon nearly 174,000 miles behind, according to NASA's online tracker.Launching April 1, 2026, from Cape Canaveral, Florida, the mission primarily serves as a test flight, with the four-person crew testing systems and hardware ahead of a future moon landing. Under the Artemis campaign, NASA intends to eventually return astronauts to the moon's surface for the first time since the Apollo missions ended in 1972.Curious exactly where and when it will land? Here's a visibility map from NASA.When does Artemis II reenter Earth's atmosphere? What time is Artemis 2 splashdown?The Orion capsule carrying NASA’s Artemis II crew is due to reenter Earth's atmosphere on Friday, April 10, 2026, and will make a water landing around 8:07 p.m. ET in the Pacific Ocean.Where will Artemis II splashdown be in California? See visibility map, NASA graphicThe Artemis II astronauts' Orion capsule is scheduled to splash down off the coast of San Diego, California.What path does Artemis II landing visibility map show?Will Artemis II splashdown be livestreamed or televised?The Artemis II splashdown on Friday, April 10, 2026, will be streamed live on NASA+, the NASA app, and its YouTube channel.All NASA+ content is available to those who have the Prime Video app downloaded on any of their devices – whether a smartphone or a smart TV.Stream Artemis II splashdown on Amazon PrimeThe USA TODAY Network will also have a livestream and live coverage at floridatoday.com/space.Samantha Neely is a trending reporter for the USA TODAY NETWORK-Florida, covering pop culture, theme parks, breaking news and more.
